prompt: AKATA's 2029 row reads gross revenue 186032000.00 USD, opex 24000000.00, capex 210000000.00 and net cash flow -121123680.00. What does the JV royalty at jv_royalty_pct 15 read on that row?

Fifteen percent of 186032000.00 less the 24000000.00 opex, because a royalty is levied on the net operating income the field actually cleared.
27904800.00, fifteen percent of the 186032000.00 of sales, before any cost is seen.
Fifteen percent of the taxable income of 113127200.00, since royalty is deductible and so must be computed on the same base as tax.
explanation: Off the top means a share of sales, not of profit: 2035 pays 10998867.98 on 73325786.51 in exactly the same proportion, and 2029 pays 27904800.00 while it loses money.

prompt: On the hand-derived case the royalty is moved from 10 to 30 percent, so the year 1 royalty line rises by 20000000.00 USD. The year 1 net moves only from -7500000.00 to -17500000.00. Where did the other half go?

Into depreciation, which absorbs a larger royalty by spreading it across the schedule.
Into the working interest, which scales the royalty line before it reaches the net.
Nowhere: the engine caps the JV royalty so that only half of any change reaches the row.
explanation: Each ten points of royalty adds 10000000.00 to the royalty line and takes 5000000.00 off tax, so the net moves 5000000.00 a step, and the take still rises from 65.3846 to 88.4615 percent.

prompt: AKATA spends 210000000.00 USD in 2029 and 45000000.00 in 2030. Its depreciation column reads 21000000.00 in 2029 and 25500000.00 in every year from 2030 to 2035. Why does the line step once and then hold?

The schedule is unit-of-production and follows the oil, which falls from 2200000.00 bbl to 1850000.00 and then declines more slowly.
The 3 percent opex escalator also inflates the depreciation, and 25500000.00 is where it saturates.
A ten-year straight line starts in each spend year, so the 2030 tranche adds its own tenth from 2030.
explanation: Two tranches, two tenths, added: the line is a schedule on the spends, and it never looks at production or prices.

prompt: Over its seven rows AKATA's default schedule claims 174000000.00 of the 255000000.00 spent. What does the engine do with the rest when the field ends in 2035?
options: It writes the gap off in 2035 as a terminal deduction, which is why the 2035 tax is only 3267865.37.
Nothing. There is no terminal write-off, so the unused deductions are simply never taken.
It carries the gap forward as loss_carryforward on the last row, where a later run could claim it.

explanation: A slow schedule leaves value on the table when the field is short, and total tax of 148425219.46 is the cost of it; the seven-year schedule claims 248571428.57 and pays 119700211.23.

No, because the five-year schedule claims 9000000.00 in 2034 that the one-year schedule never sees.

prompt: A reader's hand-built AKATA ledger shows a 2029 net that is 21000000.00 USD below -121123680.00 and a 2031 net that is 25500000.00 below 64468245.07. Which convention did they break?
options: They deducted capex from the tax base instead of depreciation, so the 2029 tax read 0.00 and the shortfall is the missing tax.
They took the royalty off revenue less opex rather than off gross revenue, which shrinks the royalty and enlarges the tax.
They forgot the royalty deduction against tax, so the base was larger than 113127200.00 in every year.
They charged depreciation to cash.
explanation: The signature is exact: the gaps are the depreciation charges of those years, and the field comes out 174000000.00 poorer than the engine says.

prompt: AKATA's 2029 taxable income is 186032000.00 less 27904800.00, less 24000000.00, less 21000000.00, which is 113127200.00 USD, and tax at 40 percent is 45250880.00. Why does a year that nets -121123680.00 pay any tax at all?
options: Capex is not deductible when spent; only its depreciation of 21000000.00 is, so the tax authority sees a year that earned 113127200.00.
Because the JV tax is levied on gross revenue and the deductions only reduce the royalty.
Because the loss carryforward kill switch is on by default under JV, so a loss year is clamped at zero and taxed as though it had earned its gross revenue.
Because capex lands in December and the tax is assessed on the year before it arrives.
explanation: The cash view and the tax view disagree, and both are printed; the loss columns read 0.00 because no AKATA base ever went negative.

prompt: With jv_tax_rate_pct set to 85 the hand-derived case prints year 1 net -35250000.00, year 2 net 14750000.00 and take 115.7692 percent. What does the take say?

prompt: loss_offset_used and loss_carryforward read 0.00 on every AKATA row. Why?

No AKATA year's taxable income goes negative; the smallest base is 8169663.42 in 2035.

The engine deducts the 210000000.00 of capex from the base in 2029 and reports the resulting loss elsewhere.
explanation: The base shrinks every year as revenue falls and opex escalates, but it stays positive, so nothing is carried and the kill switch never matters.

prompt: Under AKATA's flat 15 percent royalty and 40 percent tax, scaling the volumes to the interest first would give the same net as scaling the results afterward. Why does the engine still insist on scaling inside?
